body:
**Does not reproduce on current `main` (5479453a7), built from source today.**

Your exact remote configuration — same segment (`auto_grown_20250703034159599`), same volume, `--scale 1 -g 0 -n 1 --zarr-output` — completed 29/29 tile rows in 3m20s, exit 0, and wrote a populated 6-level pyramid (1,096 chunks, 14.3 MB, blosc/lz4). The `--tif-output` control also completed.

Your repro pins `ghcr.io/scrollprize/villa/volume-cartographer:edge`, which still ships the **2026-05-13 build** — both `:edge` and `:main`, re-measured from the registry 2026-08-31 (#1588 tracks this; #1619 was the publishing fix, closed unmerged for slot reasons). So the segfault lives in a 3.5-month-old binary; the zarr writer has changed since. Suggest retesting on a current build — the GitHub release `latest` ships 2026-08-30 binaries — before treating this as live.

*AI-assisted (Claude), human-directed account — all numbers above are from today's runs, not inferred.*

Another data point, in case it helps: same crash with `--zarr-output` on the PHerc0846A 2.403 µm scan.

Image: `ghcr.io/scrollprize/villa/volume-cartographer@sha256:bad516f66001abca759454cc43e4fd11e5b19aa55d36bdc2043817291c8083c4` (pulled as `:edge` on 2026-10-03). Host: Windows 11 + Docker Desktop (WSL2), 30 GB RAM for the VM.

Patch: ~0.5 cm², 20 generations, grown with `vc_grow_seg_from_seed` on the m7-L2 surface prediction (level-2 coordinates).

```
vc_render_tifxyz --volume /work/render_scratch \
  --remote-url s3://vesuvius-challenge-open-data/PHerc0846A/volumes/20260319102732-2.403um-0.2m-77keV-masked.zarr \
  --segmentation /work/patches/<patch>/auto_grown_<...> --zarr-output /work/patches/<patch>/sv.zarr \
  --scale 1 --group-idx 0 --scale-segmentation 4 --num-slices 65 --cache-gb 8 \
  --voxel-size 2.403 --voxel-unit micrometer --prefetch-remote
```

- The prefetch plan reports `27/27 rows, 10400 chunks`, then the process aborts with `corrupted size vs. prev_size`.
- A retry hung at 0 % CPU after the container had pulled ~31 GB (similar to #1611).
- `--flip-normals` is `unrecognised option` in this image.

Workaround I ended up using: a small Python renderer that streams only the raw chunks around each output tile's shell, writing zarr in the published surface-volume layout ([render_tifxyz_light.py](https://github.com/alexxxmur/vesuvius-pherc0846a-2p4um/blob/main/scripts/render_tifxyz_light.py)).
- It did the same patch with 4.7 GB of downloads.
- On PHerc0139 w043, rendering the same mesh and window, it matches the team surface volume with r = 0.993–0.994 for every slice. Its slice order is the reverse of vc_render's.

I tried to reproduce this on current `main` and couldn't. I think it's fixed by 502dbc06 ("vc-render-tifxyz: fix segfault due to uninitialized buffers", 2026-06-24), and the crash only happens because of the stale `:edge` image.

**Why the original repro still crashes:** both reports in this thread used `ghcr.io/scrollprize/villa/volume-cartographer:edge`. That tag (and `:main`) still points at the 2026-05-13 build of 1e3f4c02 (amd64 digest `sha256:b2509de2…`). 502dbc06 came after it: 1e3f4c02 is an ancestor of 502dbc06, and 502dbc06 is in current `main`. See #1588 for the stale images.

**What I ran:** release build 8aa507c (2026-10-18), with the same segment (`auto_grown_20250703034159599`), the same PHerc1447 8.64 µm masked volume streamed from S3, and `--scale 1 -g 0`. One difference: `--remote-url` is deprecated, so I passed the URL to `-v` instead.

```bash
vc_render_tifxyz \
  -v https://vesuvius-challenge-open-data.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/PHerc1447/volumes/20250521151220-8.640um-1.2m-116keV-masked.zarr \
  -s auto_grown_20250703034159599 \
  --scale 1 -g 0 -n 65 --cache-gb 4 \
  --zarr-output out/n65.zarr
```

| Platform | n | Result |
|---|---|---|
| macOS arm64 (release .app) | 1 | exit 0, ~5 min, 17 MB |
| macOS arm64 (release .app) | 65 | exit 0, ~2.5 min, 890 MB |
| Linux x86_64 (release AppImage, Ubuntu 24.04 container) | 65 | exit 0, 81 s, 890 MB |

Output on both platforms is a full 6-level pyramid, shape `[65, 3700, 5460]`, chunks `[65, 128, 128]`, uint8/blosc-lz4. Chunk counts per level are 784 / 223 / 65 / 20 / 7 / 3, and the two platforms produced exactly the same set of chunk keys.

**Cross-platform check:** I decompressed 20 level-0 chunks (21.3M voxels) from each platform and compared them:
- 0.19% of voxels differ, by at most 1 grey level
- the nonzero voxel count is identical (18,838,638)

So this is float rounding between arm64 and x86_64, not corruption.

Unless someone can still reproduce this on a current build, I think this can be closed as fixed by 502dbc06. The `:edge` image is still the trap (#1588 / #1982).
